primary_topics: Chapter 12 of 'Love God, Serve Man' -- the transcript of CJP's extemporaneous, largely Tagalog talk of May 19, 1991 before some 5,000 people of Smokey Mountain gathered at the Folk Arts Theater as the General Assembly of the Sambayanang Kristiano, bringing the message of the Second Plenary Council of the Philippines to the masses.

What a Plenary Council is and what PCP II was -- a month-long lawmaking gathering at the San Carlos Pastoral Complex of 489 participants, including 156 lay people, the first time in the 2,000-year history of the Church that laymen joined its lawmaking, and an experience he calls humbling and unforgettable.

PCP II's first aspiration, RENEWAL or PAGBABAGO: a conversion of heart and of mind for a people who are Christian in church but violent, corrupt and poor outside it, requiring a faith that is Christ-centered, rooted in the Word of God, inculturated as authentically Filipino, and others-oriented.

PCP II's second aspiration, SOCIAL TRANSFORMATION -- the proclamation of a 'Church of the Poor' that is at once a declaration of identity, mission, constituency and commitment -- together with the redefinition of 'Church' as all the faithful, which is why PCP II recognizes the 'empowerment of the laity' or, in simple language, 'people power.'
sub_topics: Thanks to his hosts -- Pangulong Edmar A. Jimenez, Uma-aktong Pangulong Estelita Bianes, Pangkalahatang Kalihim Luzviminda Salcedo and spiritual director Fr. Ben Beltran -- and the reminder that whoever they are, 'Tayo pong lahat ay anak ng Diyos.'

The opening riddle of the two theme songs: the song of those in hell is 'SANA' -- wishing they had loved their families and neighbors while alive -- while the song of those in heaven is 'Osana,' the difference being the 'O' that stands for the Ostia, the body of Christ that draws us near to heaven.
His three announced questions: what a Plenary Council is, what two aspirations of PCP II the gathering should know, and how those aspirations can be lived.

The nature of a Plenary Council: a gathering of bishops and ecclesiastical authorities to make new laws and renew the faith, whose decrees become church law once approved by the Holy See; the first Philippine council was held in 1953, attended by bishops and priests only, when the population was 27 million against 60 million now.

PCP II's composition and significance: convened by the Pope at the instance of the CBCP, it drew 489 participants -- 93 archbishops and bishops, 226 priests, 14 religious sisters and brothers and 156 lay people -- meeting daily from half past six in the morning until six at night for more than a month.

His own diffidence and growth: he 'felt very unworthy' and at first would not speak, unqualified to debate theology with 'the best minds of our Church,' until the encouragement of the bishops and prayers to the Holy Spirit gave him courage to debate.

The SK's own aspirations, briefed to him by coordinator Cris Harina -- 'the SPIRITUAL' cleansing of self-centeredness and 'the ECONOMIC' uplifting of living standards through cooperatives -- which he maps onto PCP II's RENEWAL and SOCIAL TRANSFORMATION.

The paradox behind RENEWAL: the only Christian country in Asia is among the most violent, graft-prone and poorest -- are we Christians only inside the church, becoming 'pagans and barbarians' once we leave it?

The four requirements of a re-educated heart and mind: Christ-centered (devotion to Mary and the saints must never displace Him -- 'Jesus lives!'); rooted in the Word of God, which PCP II now requires the faithful to read and live; inculturated and authentically Filipino, which is why he praises the SK for using Filipino; and others-oriented, since 'A self-seeking, self-oriented faith is no faith,' per the two great commandments.

The Church of the Poor explained in Tagalog: it does not mean the Church wants us poor but 'gusto tayong mahango sa kahirapan' -- lifted out of poverty by livelihood training and solidarity rather than by dole-outs.

PCP II's own four-part definition of the Church of the Poor -- evangelical poverty, defense of the poor's rights even at the cost of persecution, the poor as evangelizers themselves, and a Church 'where no one is so poor as to have nothing to give' -- with the first Jerusalem community, 'united, heart and soul,' as its ideal, rendered in Tagalog for his audience.

Bro. Sonny de los Reyes's four-fold reading of the proclamation: a declaration of identity (Christ identifying with the least, Matt. 25:40,45), of mission (Luke 4:18, glad tidings to the poor), of constituency (the Beatitudes, Matt. 5:3 and Luke 6:20), and of commitment, entailing an emptying of attachment to wealth, prestige, power and privilege (Philippians; 2 Cor. 8:9).

The redefinition of 'Church': no longer the building or the hierarchy but all the faithful -- 'you and me, all of us' -- so that calling the Philippine Church a Church of the Poor binds rich and poor, adults and children, all equal in dignity and mission.

Lay empowerment as people power: because the faithful now constitute the Church, PCP II recognizes the 'empowerment of the laity,' which in simple language is the 'people power' the faithful started 'in Mendiola, in EDSA,' and which is present in the Folk Arts Theater gathering itself.

The closing parable of the wounded healer, told by Justice Hugo Gutierrez: a great physician with an incurable wound goes to the pool of Bethesda, and a former patient begs him not to dip his hand, since 'it is only the injured that knows the pain of the wounded' -- God sometimes permits suffering so that we may heal others.

one_paragraph_summary: Chapter 12 of 'Love God, Serve Man' is the transcript of CJP's extemporaneous, mostly Tagalog talk of May 19, 1991, delivered to some 5,000 people of Smokey Mountain gathered at the Folk Arts Theater as the General Assembly of the Sambayanang Kristiano, and meant to carry the message of the Second Plenary Council of the Philippines to the masses. He opened with a riddle -- the theme song of those in hell is 'SANA,' of those in heaven 'Osana,' the difference being the 'O' for the Ostia -- then set three questions: what a Plenary Council is, what two aspirations of PCP II mattered most, and how they could be lived. He explained that a plenary council makes church law once approved by the Holy See; that the first Philippine council of 1953 admitted only bishops and priests; and that PCP II, convened at the instance of the CBCP, gathered 489 participants including 156 lay people, the first time in 2,000 years that laymen shared in the Church's lawmaking -- an experience he called humbling and unforgettable, admitting he felt unworthy and spoke only after the bishops encouraged him. He then gave PCP II's twin aspirations. RENEWAL, or pagbabago, demanded conversion of heart and mind from a people Christian inside church yet violent and corrupt outside it, and required a faith that is Christ-centered, rooted in the Word of God, inculturated as authentically Filipino, and others-oriented, since 'A self-seeking, self-oriented faith is no faith.' SOCIAL TRANSFORMATION meant the proclamation of a 'Church of the Poor' -- not a Church wanting people poor but one lifting them from poverty through livelihood and solidarity rather than dole-outs -- which he read, following Bro. Sonny de los Reyes, as a declaration of identity, mission, constituency and commitment. Because 'Church' now means all the faithful, PCP II recognizes lay empowerment, the people power begun in Mendiola and EDSA. He closed with Justice Hugo Gutierrez's parable of the wounded healer at the pool of Bethesda.
